    Relative cochains compute ordinary Hochschild cohomology in degree two #

    weights-and-parameters.tex: "we use normalized cochains relative to the split vertex algebra […] these relative cochains compute ordinary Hochschild cohomology." The formalization works with normalized S-relative cochains (IsRel₁, IsRel₂). This file proves the claim for HH²(Λ)_q, the only Hochschild group the paper uses:

    • every Hochschild two-cocycle of internal degree q is cohomologous, by a degree-q coboundary, to a normalized S-relative one (exists_rel_cohomologous);
    • a normalized S-relative two-cochain that is the coboundary of some degree-q one-cochain is the coboundary of a normalized S-relative one (exists_rel_of_cobdry).

    So the relative classes are exactly the ordinary classes. In particular the spanning condition on HH²(Λ)_{>0} (Theorem 7.7, Proposition 7.6) reads the same in both forms (span_rel_iff; the hypotheses of Theorem 7.7 in the ordinary form give FamilyHyp, familyHyp_of_ordinary), and so does the nonvanishing of a class (rel_isCobdry_iff).

        A normalized S-relative two-cochain is a relative coboundary iff it is an ordinary coboundary (in internal degree q): the nonvanishing of a class reads the same in both forms.

        FamilyHyp V μ qd

        The hypotheses of Theorem 7.7 with HH² as ordinary Hochschild cohomology: if the μ_i are normalized S-relative of positive degrees, m + Σ t_i μ_i is associative, and their classes span the ordinary HH²(Λ)_q for every q > 0, then FamilyHyp holds.
